title: Choose what we can see.
intro: One person. Five frames. What do you gain as you get closer, and what do you leave out?
question: Before changing the frame, predict which view will help you understand the place. Which will help you read a small gesture?
transfer: Find a moment in a game you know. Describe the framing before you describe the emotion. What information does that view give the player?
terms: Extreme wide shot
A subject is small in a much larger setting.
Wide shot
The whole subject and the space around it are visible.
Medium shot
Usually a person from about the waist up, with some context.
Close-up
The face or another subject fills much of the frame.
Extreme close-up
A small detail fills the frame, such as an eye or a hand.
videos: Learn: All Camera Shot Sizes Explained
Look for the boundary of each frame, not a universal emotional meaning.
Find a cut from a broad view to a face. What information changed?
source: Session 2 first-meeting board, August 26. The shot-scale annotation uses Up.

title: Give color a purpose.
intro: Keep the arrangement. Change the palette. Then change saturation on its own. A feeling is a reading you can explain, not a color law.
question: Predict what will happen to the scene when you remove its color. What still guides your eye?
transfer: Choose three colors for an imagined game location. Explain a job for each. Try a different palette for the same location and compare.
terms: Color script
A sequence of color plans showing how palette and mood change across a story.
Palette
A selected range of colors used together.
Warm / cool
Color relationships often described as reds, oranges and yellows versus blues and greens. Meanings depend on context and culture.
Lighting
The direction, color and quality of light in a scene.
Saturation
The intensity of a color, from gray to vivid.
Value
How light or dark a color is, independent of its hue.
High-key / low-key
High-key lighting usually has low contrast and few deep shadows. Low-key lighting has strong contrast and substantial shadow.
Motivated / stylized light
Motivated light suggests a source in the world. Stylized light may serve an expressive purpose without a visible source.
Hard / soft light
Hard light produces sharper shadow edges; soft light produces gradual edges.
Color and culture
A color can carry different associations for different people and contexts. State your reading and evidence.
videos: Pause on two settings. Compare their palettes and values.
Look at light and shadow on one subject. What is being emphasized?
source: Session 3 terms/media sheets. Gordon confirmed the full GTA VI extended look was shown; the guide does not infer which other planned activities were completed.

title: Move for a reason.
intro: A turn and a journey are different. Try a small camera diagram. See what moves before deciding what it means.
question: Which move changes the camera’s position? Which changes only the direction it points? Predict, then try both.
transfer: Watch a moving shot. Finish: “The camera moves so that we can see ___.” Then imagine holding it still. What would we lose or gain?
terms: Pan
Turn the camera left or right from a fixed position.
Tilt
Turn the camera up or down from a fixed position.
Dolly
Move the camera through space toward or away from a subject. This changes perspective; a zoom changes the lens view without moving the camera.
Crane / boom
Raise or lower the camera’s position through space.
Tracking / following
Travel with a moving subject. A pan may follow a subject too, but the camera itself stays in one place.
Dutch angle
Roll the frame so its horizon is tilted. Different from a tilt, which points the camera up or down.
Parallax
Nearby and faraway objects appear to shift by different amounts as the viewpoint moves.
Focal length
A lens property affecting angle of view. Perspective also depends on camera position; a longer lens alone does not change that position.
Handheld / locked-off
Handheld includes movement from a held camera. Locked-off keeps the camera fixed. Either can serve a deliberate purpose.
Motivated camera move
A move that serves something in the scene, such as following an action or revealing information.
videos: Find one move. Name what it reveals rather than only saying it looks cool.
Consider how the physical cost of a move can shape its purpose.
source: Session 4 shared source session4.py and student terms/media sheets.

title: Give the eye a path.
intro: Brighten a doorway. Move two friends apart. Change which layer is sharp. Compare the visible result with your intention.
question: What draws your eye first? Can you change that without moving the objects?
transfer: Design a frame for a player who needs to find a partner. Ask someone what they notice before telling them your intention.
terms: Composition
How elements are arranged inside a frame.
Visual hierarchy
The order in which elements attract attention.
Negative space
The less occupied space around and between subjects.
Depth
The sense of near and far.
Depth of field
The range of distances that appears acceptably sharp.
Establishing shot
A shot that helps us understand a setting or spatial relationship.
source: Official Version B recap: six interactive lessons, 34 terms, practice and mood-board studio preserved in full.

title: Make time mean something.
intro: Keep the four shots. Change their durations. Then hold durations equal and change order. One variable at a time helps you see why an edit feels different.
question: If the same four shots stay in the same order, does a longer hold create another cut? Count the boundaries.
transfer: Describe a ten-second sequence for your world. Choose one moment to hold. Explain what that time gives the viewer.
terms: Cut
A change from one shot to the next.
Pacing
The rhythm and speed of the unfolding sequence.
Montage
Meaning made through a sequence of images placed together; it can compress time and need not be fast.
Continuity
Consistency across shots that helps a viewer follow space, time or action.
Beat
A meaningful moment or rhythm unit.
Cutaway
A shot away from the main action, often supplying a detail or reaction.
Wipe
A transition with a moving boundary that reveals the next image.
source: Official Version B student Editing Lab, September14. Timing and ordering isolated; transitions, terminology and reflections retained.
